title: The Flying Roll and Wickedness
overview: Zechariah chapter 5 presents two vivid prophetic visions that reveal God's judgment against sin and wickedness among His people. The first vision depicts a flying scroll symbolizing a curse that will sweep across the earth, targeting thieves and those who swear falsely by God's name. The second vision reveals a woman representing wickedness confined within an ephah, a measure of grain, which is then carried away to the land of Shinar to be established there. These visions emphasize the certainty of divine judgment on sin and the removal of evil from the community. The chapter powerfully underscores God's holiness and justice, warning that sin brings destruction and must be dealt with decisively for the restoration of His people.
structure:
**Verses 1-4: The Vision of the Flying Roll.** The prophet sees a large flying scroll, which the angel explains is a curse that will go forth over the whole earth, specifically condemning thieves and those who swear falsely. This curse will enter and consume the houses of the guilty, symbolizing God's judgment on sin within the community.

**Verses 5-8: The Vision of the Ephah and the Woman.** The prophet is shown an ephah, a grain measure, containing a woman who represents wickedness. The woman is sealed inside with a heavy lead weight, indicating containment and judgment upon sin.

**Verses 9-11: The Removal of Wickedness.** Two women with stork-like wings lift the ephah between heaven and earth and carry it to the land of Shinar, where a house will be built for it. This symbolizes the removal and exile of wickedness from Israel to a place of judgment and separation.

keyVerses.text: Then said he unto me, This is the curse that goeth forth over the face of the whole earth: for every one that stealeth shall be cut off as on this side according to it; and every one that sweareth shall be cut off as on that side according to it.
keyVerses.significance: This verse reveals the universal scope of God's judgment against sin, specifically theft and false oaths, highlighting the holiness of God and the seriousness of covenant faithfulness.

keyVerses.text: I will bring it forth, saith the LORD of hosts, and it shall enter into the house of the thief, and into the house of him that sweareth falsely by my name: and it shall remain in the midst of his house, and shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.
keyVerses.significance: God declares His active role in bringing judgment directly into the homes of sinners, emphasizing that no sin is hidden from His sight and that judgment will be thorough and consuming.

keyVerses.text: And he said, This is wickedness. And he cast it into the midst of the ephah; and he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof.
keyVerses.significance: This verse identifies the woman in the ephah as wickedness and shows that sin is confined and weighed down, symbolizing God's control over evil and the certainty of its judgment.

keyVerses.text: And he said unto me, To build it an house in the land of Shinar: and it shall be established, and set there upon her own base.
keyVerses.significance: The removal of wickedness to Shinar (Babylon) signifies the exile and separation of sin from God's people, pointing to the consequences of rebellion and the hope of purification.

characters.name: The Angel
characters.description: The angel serves as the divine guide and interpreter of the visions, explaining the symbolic meanings of the flying roll and the ephah to Zechariah, revealing God's judgment and purposes.

characters.name: The Woman (Wickedness)
characters.description: Personified as a woman sitting inside the ephah, she symbolizes wickedness or sin confined and weighed down, representing the moral corruption that must be removed from the land.

characters.name: Zechariah
characters.description: The prophet who receives and records these visions, serving as God's messenger to communicate warnings and hope to the post-exilic community.

themes.description: The chapter emphasizes God's active judgment against sin, particularly theft and false oaths, demonstrating that God holds His people accountable for covenant faithfulness.
Wickedness is depicted as a woman confined and removed from the land, symbolizing God's intention to purge evil from His people and restore holiness.
The curse on thieves and oath-breakers highlights the importance of living in accordance with God's covenant, reflecting His holy standards for His people.
The transportation of wickedness to Shinar points to the theme of exile as a consequence of sin, a motif that runs throughout the prophetic literature.

historicalContext: Zechariah prophesied during the post-exilic period, approximately 520-518 BC, after the Jewish people returned from Babylonian captivity. The community was rebuilding Jerusalem and the temple under Persian rule, facing challenges of spiritual renewal and social reform. The visions reflect concerns about internal corruption and the need for holiness among God's restored people. The land of Shinar mentioned here refers to ancient Babylon, symbolizing a place of exile and judgment. Understanding the political subjugation under Persia and the cultural memory of exile is essential to grasp the urgency of these prophetic warnings.

theologicalInterpretations.description: This perspective sees the flying roll as God's sovereign judgment on sin that must be purged for the community's covenant faithfulness. The woman in the ephah represents corporate wickedness that God confines and removes, emphasizing God's holiness and justice.

Dispensational interpreters often see the visions as symbolic of God's judgment on Israel's unfaithfulness, with the removal of wickedness foreshadowing future eschatological purging before the millennial kingdom.

Early church interpreters viewed the flying roll as the law condemning sin and the woman as the personification of evil or the synagogue of Satan, highlighting the spiritual battle between righteousness and wickedness.

application: Recognize that God sees all sin, even what is hidden in our homes, and calls for repentance and holiness.
Avoid theft and false oaths, understanding these sins bring serious consequences under God's covenant.
Confess and confront personal and communal wickedness to allow God to purify His people.
Trust in God's justice that will ultimately remove evil and restore righteousness.
Pray for spiritual renewal and the strength to live faithfully in covenant obedience.
Remember that God’s judgment serves to protect the community and maintain His holy standards.
conclusion: Zechariah chapter 5 powerfully illustrates God's intolerance of sin and His commitment to purging wickedness from His people. Through vivid symbolic visions, the chapter warns that theft and falsehood bring inevitable judgment, while wickedness will be confined and removed. This serves as a solemn reminder for believers to uphold covenant faithfulness and holiness. The chapter encourages self-examination, repentance, and reliance on God's justice, assuring that evil will not remain but will be dealt with decisively, paving the way for restoration and blessing.
timeline: c. 520 BC - Post-Exilic Period during Persian Rule

definitions.definition: An ancient Hebrew unit of dry measure, approximately equivalent to 22 liters or about half a bushel, used here symbolically to contain wickedness.
A large unit of weight, often used for precious metals; here a 'talent of lead' symbolizes a heavy weight sealing the ephah.
An ancient name for the region of Babylon, representing exile and a place of judgment in biblical prophecy.
A large scroll seen flying through the air in the vision, symbolizing a divine curse or judgment that is active and pervasive.
Breaking an oath made in God's name, considered a serious violation of covenant trust and holiness.

outline.heading: The Flying Roll and Its Curse
outline.description: Zechariah sees a large flying scroll representing a curse against thieves and false swearers, which will enter and consume their homes, symbolizing God's judgment on covenant unfaithfulness.

outline.heading: The Ephah and the Woman of Wickedness
outline.description: The prophet is shown an ephah containing a woman symbolizing wickedness, sealed with a heavy lead weight, illustrating the containment and judgment of sin.

outline.heading: The Removal of Wickedness to Shinar
outline.description: Two women with wings carry the ephah between heaven and earth to the land of Shinar, where a house will be built for wickedness, symbolizing exile and separation from God's people.
